question: Should OpenClaw add a Slack outbound DM recipient allowlist, and should that contract be Slack-specific or part of a shared channel recipient-policy design?
rationale: The request adds public config and outbound authorization semantics in a security-sensitive channel path, and current docs intentionally define `allowFrom` as inbound access rather than recipient authorization.

options.title: Add Explicit Slack Outbound Policy
options.body: Introduce a Slack-owned optional recipient allowlist, document its account/wildcard semantics, and enforce it across explicit and agent-originated Slack DM sends.

options.title: Wait For Shared Recipient Policy
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers design one channel-agnostic outbound recipient policy shared by Slack, WhatsApp, and other DM-capable channels.

options.title: Decline Outbound ACL
options.body: Close this as not planned if maintainers want the trusted-operator model and existing tool/session policies to remain the only guardrails for explicit outbound sends.

recommendation.title: Add Explicit Slack Outbound Policy
recommendation.body: Introduce a Slack-owned optional recipient allowlist, document its account/wildcard semantics, and enforce it across explicit and agent-originated Slack DM sends.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has recent Slack DM policy/docs history and already handled the related outbound-security triage, making them the best available decision owner from the history trail.
